title: Binary F1 Score
statement: Implement `f1_score(y_true, y_pred)` for binary labels where 1 is the positive class. Compute precision and recall from true positives, false positives, and false negatives. Return the harmonic mean 2PR / (P + R). If there are no true positives, return 0.0.
constraints: Zero true positives yields 0.0, not an exception

approaches.name: Confusion counts
approaches.explanation: F1 is the harmonic mean, so both precision and recall must be high.

editorial: Precision asks how many predicted positives were real. Recall asks how many real positives were found. F1 = 2PR / (P + R) is high only when both are high, which is why it is the default on imbalanced classification. When tp is 0, precision or recall hits a zero denominator; the conventional score is 0. This implementation is binary and treats label 1 as positive. Multiclass F1 needs an averaging policy (macro, micro, or weighted) that you should state before coding.
